question: Should OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests across one reviewer instance, including cached ask, timeout, and error outcomes, or should the cache scope be narrower?
rationale: Exec auto-review sits on the process approval boundary; the implementation is plausible, but reusing a prior model verdict changes one-request-one-review semantics and needs explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve per-instance full-input memo
options.body: Allow the bounded reviewer-instance cache once real proof is added, treating repeated identical exec review inputs as one deterministic reviewer decision.

options.title: Narrow the cache
options.body: Require the branch to cache only parsed low-risk allow-once decisions or key by the exact reviewer prompt for a smaller approval-boundary change.

options.title: Keep one-review-per-request
options.body: Reject memoization and accept repeated reviewer cost to preserve a fresh model review for every exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve per-instance full-input memo
recommendation.body: Allow the bounded reviewer-instance cache once real proof is added, treating repeated identical exec review inputs as one deterministic reviewer decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame on the affected reviewer and both host call sites makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the approval-boundary decision.
